scenes.title:
Familiar shape.
Different heart.
cues: This looks like an Arduino Uno. But the chip at its heart is something different.
Meet Micro Petal: an Uno-format board built around a Puya P Y thirty-two microcontroller.

scenes.title:
Start with F071.
Leave room for F072.
labels: F072 software support is not implemented
cues: The initial target is the F zero seventy-one. The board also accommodates the F zero seventy-two.
That is a hardware option, not a claim that the software already supports both.

scenes.title:
Write a sketch.
Make it blink.
cues: An experimental Arduino core and Platform I O platform bring familiar sketches to the board.
One detail matters immediately: the on-board L E D turns on when its pin goes low.

scenes.title: Know your pins.
cues: The Uno outline does not mean every shield is plug and play.
Serial transmit is on D two, not D one. I squared C uses the dedicated S D A and S C L pins.

scenes.title:
Check JP3.
Select 3.3 volts.
cues: Before powering this revision, read the jumper guide.
The fitted transceiver needs three point three volts, but J P three defaults to five. Change and verify the jumper with power disconnected.

scenes.eyebrow: OPEN THE REPO. FOLLOW THE BUILD.
scenes.title:
MicroPetal.
Ready to explore.
labels: Physical upload and runtime validation pending
cues: The repository includes the hardware, software, examples, and getting-started guides.
The software passes its build checks. Physical upload and runtime validation are still ahead. Follow the project on GitHub.
